A loyalty balance CANNOT be reset on this platform — vc-module-loyalty exposes the operation log read-only, with no balance set/debit API — so every balance figure below is a RELATIVE DELTA against a value read immediately before the action, never an absolute number. Title: Organization mode — writing the mode setting takes effect on the very next loyalty read, with no cached-setting lag
Preconditions: Store {{STORE_ID}} is in Organization mode — the store setting Loyalty.LoyaltyBalanceCalculationMode reads "Organization". This is NOT the ambient state of the environment (the platform default is "Customer", which the rest of the loyalty corpus assumes), so the run sets it before this suite and restores it after; a case here that finds the store in Customer mode must report BLOCKED rather than assert. The outlet's pooled balance is non-zero and strictly greater than member A's own personal (Customer-scope) balance — that inequality is what makes the scope change observable in a single read. This case OWNS the store mode for its duration: it reads, writes "Customer", reads again IMMEDIATELY with no wait, and restores "Organization". The mode setting cannot be read back as a scored assertion: the settings-v2 tenant endpoint answers a dictionary keyed by the dotted setting name, and the runner's path grammar splits a path on "." before matching, so "body.Loyalty.LoyaltyBalanceCalculationMode" cannot resolve. The mode is therefore verified by its EFFECT, not by reading the value back — do not "repair" this into a dotted path filter. A loyalty balance CANNOT be reset on this platform — vc-module-loyalty exposes the operation log read-only, with no balance set/debit API — so every balance figure below is a RELATIVE DELTA against a value read immediately before the action, never an absolute number.

[GQL-EXEC me_a]
[GQL-CAPTURE me_a.data.me.id → USER_ID]
[GQL-OP bal_org]

Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] the hypothesis is that IsOrganizationBalanceCalculationMode reads the store through a service that serves a cached store entity, while the settings-v2 write goes through a different endpoint that need not invalidate it
[API] a merchant cannot be told WHEN a scope change applies if it depends on an unspecified cache eviction; the answer this case produces is a release-note fact, not only a verdict
